content: Type 1 Diabetes is an autoimmune condition where the immune system mistakenly attacks the insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas, leading to insulin deficiency. The American Diabetes Association (ADA) provides guidelines and resources for understanding and managing Type 1 Diabetes. Autoimmunity can also play a role in Type 2 Diabetes, although it is less common than in Type 1 Diabetes. Patients undergoing treatment with immune checkpoint inhibitors may experience immune-related adverse reactions. These reactions are more likely to occur in individuals who carry high-risk HLA-DR4 alleles.
